skill.name: animate-expo
skill.description: Build smooth, accessible React Native animations for Expo apps with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router, and haptic feedback.
skill.summary: Design and implement responsive Expo motion that stays fluid on real devices.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Mobile animations often stutter, ignore accessibility, or conflict with gestures. This skill designs Expo motion with suitable tools, timing, threading, and device checks.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates whether an interaction should animate based on frequency and purpose.
Selects Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router, Lottie, or Skia for specific motion needs.
Implements gesture-driven motion with velocity handoff, springs, rubber-banding, and interruption handling.
Creates press feedback, sheets, swipe actions, headers, list entrances, keyboard motion, tabs, transitions, and toasts.
Adds reduced-motion behavior, touch-target guidance, and coordinated visual and haptic feedback.
Diagnoses common Expo animation setup and performance problems.
limitations: Device feel, gesture timing, and haptic quality still require testing on physical hardware.
The guidance targets Expo and modern React Native projects using Reanimated 4.
Some navigation, sheet, menu, and haptic behaviors differ between iOS and Android.
It does not replace product decisions about when motion supports the user experience.

use_cases.title: Add responsive press feedback
use_cases.description: Create subtle press motion with accessible touch targets and suitable timing.

use_cases.title: Design gesture-driven interactions
use_cases.description: Build interruptible sheets or swipe actions with velocity-aware settling.

use_cases.title: Fix animation performance
use_cases.description: Review thread usage, animated properties, runtime setup, and device verification.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a simple state change
prompt_templates.prompt: Add subtle press feedback to my Expo button. Keep it accessible, explain the motion choice, and provide the implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a screen transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure an Expo Router transition for this modal flow. Respect reduced motion and preserve native navigation gestures.

prompt_templates.title: Build a dismissible sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a draggable in-screen sheet using Reanimated and Gesture Handler. Include velocity projection, interruption handling, and coordinated haptics.

prompt_templates.title: Audit motion performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Expo animation files for dropped-frame risks. Correct thread crossings, layout-heavy properties, gesture conflicts, and accessibility gaps.

output_examples.input: Add animation when a settings toggle changes.
output_examples.output: Gate: frequent interaction, so use a subtle state transition. Use a short UI-thread color and scale change, with reduced motion preserving the color cue.

output_examples.input: Make this card swipe away when deleted.
output: Use a horizontal pan gesture with a declared axis.
Project release velocity to decide whether deletion commits.
Settle with a spring or complete with a short timing animation.
Test slow drags, fast flicks, interruptions, and vertical scrolling on a device.

output_examples.input: The collapsing header stutters on Android.
output_examples.output: Keep the header height fixed and animate translated content with opacity. Drive values on the UI thread and verify the release build on the slowest supported Android device.

best_practices: Name the animation purpose before choosing a tool or writing code.
Keep continuous gesture and scroll updates on the UI thread.
Test reduced motion and release performance on supported physical devices.
anti_patterns: Do not update React state on every gesture or scroll frame.
Do not animate layout-heavy properties when transforms and opacity can express the motion.
Do not use haptics as the only feedback or trigger them every frame.

faq.question: Which Expo animation tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router, expo-haptics, and selected specialized libraries when appropriate.

faq.question: Can it create gesture-driven animations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers drags, swipes, velocity projection, spring settling, interruption, axis conflicts, and runtime handoff.

faq.question: Does it support reduced motion?
faq.answer: Yes. It keeps essential state cues while reducing translation, scale, parallax, and overshoot.

faq.question: Can it fix stuttering animations?
faq.answer: It identifies React rerenders, runtime crossings, layout passes, setup errors, and unsuitable testing environments.

faq.question: Does it work for web animation?
faq.answer: No. This skill focuses on React Native and Expo mobile applications.

faq.question: Is simulator testing enough?
faq.answer: No. Gesture feel, haptics, and frame performance require release testing on physical supported devices.
